in.other_title: AI debate helps human judges with strong prior beliefs assess controversial COVID-19 and climate claims
in.rationale: Arnesen et al. say they focus only on reading comprehension with an information-access expertise gap. Rahman et al. report debate beats consultancy by 4-10% for human judges on COVID-19 and climate claims; the debaters are two AI systems and the Study I judges are humans. Rahman et al.'s Study I judges were recruited with either mainstream or skeptical beliefs on claims where people hold strong prior beliefs, and the improvement was most significant for mainstream-belief judges, so the study concerns whether debate can guide biased judges, while Arnesen et al.'s expertise gap relies on asymmetric access to textual information; Study II uses AI judges.

text: The authors state that their judge-debater expertise gap, based on asymmetric access to textual information, may not be the best proxy for future expertise gaps such as in reasoning abilities, and that they focus only on reading comprehension questions, for which Kenton et al.
